[1/4] Design and implement BFS shortest path finding and narrative reasoning in lattice.analysis

impact_assessment.why: Enable researchers and AI agents to trace multi-hop chains of evidence and citations connecting any two entities in the knowledge graph
impact_assessment.benefits: Provides deterministic provenance chains, explains how distant findings or papers relate, and exposes path finding across CLI, API, MCP, and Web Studio without heuristics
impact_assessment.risks: Performance on dense cycles and malformed entity references
impact_assessment.mitigation: Cycle detection via visited sets, depth capping (default 5, max 10), entity validation via validate_ref, and strict BFS shortest path guarantee

[1/3] Design and implement deterministic hypothesis generation in lattice.analysis

impact_assessment.why: Systematically translate evidence matrix coverage gaps and contradiction clusters into structured, testable scientific hypotheses for researchers and autonomous AI agents
impact_assessment.benefits: Closes the scientific discovery loop from evidence synthesis to next-experiment design with explicit independent/dependent variables and recommended study types
impact_assessment.risks: Vague or ungrounded hypotheses without clear variable extraction
impact_assessment.mitigation: Extract variables directly from opposing claim phrases and question prompts using deterministic keyword heuristic templates; zero hallucinated provenance

[1/3] Design and implement CSL-JSON bibliography parser in lattice.ingest

impact_assessment.why: Enable researchers and agents to ingest universal CSL-JSON citation bibliographies from Zotero, Mendeley, and Crossref directly into the Lattice evidence graph
impact_assessment.benefits: Expands interoperability to the predominant JSON reference format with zero third-party dependencies, preserving all metadata and study types
impact_assessment.risks: Malformed JSON payloads or missing author/date fields
impact_assessment.mitigation: Robust defensive normalization for date-parts, author arrays/literals, and study type fallback inference
